In a recent development, investors choosing between growth and stability often weigh the explosive potential of cosmetics against the steady demand for energy drinks. This comparison evaluates whether e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) or Monster Beverage (MNST -0.57%) is the better buy.

e.l.f. Beauty disrupts the traditional makeup industry by offering high-speed product innovation and prestige-quality items at accessible prices. Monster Beverage dominates the beverage coolers with its diverse energy portfolio and global scale. Both companies have delivered impressive long-term results, but they offer distinct risk and reward profiles for retail investors.

Industry observers note that e.l.f. Beauty operates in the competitive segment of consumer staples stocks, focusing on high-quality cosmetics at accessible price points. The firm sells its products through mass, drug, and specialty retail channels, including key partners like Target (TGT -0.97%), Walmart (WMT +1.51%), and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). These retail relationships account for nearly 76% of net sales, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.9 billion. This represented revenue growth of roughly 39.9% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for those 12 months was approximately $86.6 million, supported by a net margin of close to 4.5%.

Industry observers note that as of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.8x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a firm funds its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 2.3x. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $190.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 40.9% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

It has been revealed that monster Beverage functions as a holding manufacturer for major energy brands like Reign, NOS, and Bang. It primarily distributes its beverages through an extensive network of bottlers, relying on Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) as its primary global distribution partner. The company currently serves a growing number of international markets across 80 countries, leveraging this massive network to maintain its market lead.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $9.6 billion. This reflects revenue growth of approximately 20.2% over the previous year. Net income for the period was nearly $2.2 billion, resulting in a healthy net margin of approximately 22.7%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the organization carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x. This indicates that shareholder equity covers all liabilities, leaving the company with no debt relative to equity. The current ratio is nearly 3.7x, indicating the business has sufficient liquidity to cover its short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $2.0 billion.

Recent findings suggest that e.l.f. Beauty faces intense competition in its industry from multinational firms such as Coty (COTY -2.47%) and L'Oréal (LRLCF -1.17%). Because it sources the majority of its products from third-party manufacturers in China, the firm is exposed to trade policies and tariff-related risks. It must also manage rapid growth and system integrations while remaining dependent on a limited number of major retail customers, such as Target and Walmart.

In a recent development, monster Beverage relies heavily on its distribution relationship with Coca-Cola, which is vital to its international performance. The manufacturer faces significant competition in the energy drink category from PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) and other global beverage giants. Additionally, it is subject to risks related to ingredient pricing, supply chain disruptions, and evolving government regulations regarding energy drink labeling and health standards.

In a recent development, e.l.f. Beauty right now appears more attractively valued than Monster Beverage based on both its lower Forward P/E and its lower P/S ratio.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The Forward P/E compares current share price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

What sets e.l.f. apart is selling prestige-quality makeup and skincare at mass-market prices, and it introduces newly introduced products faster than the bigger beauty companies can respond. That's why I'd buy it for 2027. Growth is strong, and rhode, the skincare brand founded by Hailey Bieber that e.l.f. bought in August 2025, gives it a bigger foothold in skin care. Shoppers who keep buying small treats when budgets tighten also help the case. I'd treat this as a starter position to watch through 2027, not a stock to hold blindly. The December quarter is the first fully organic comparison, so it will show how fast e.l.f. grows once rhode sits in both periods. Beauty runs on trends, and rhode depends heavily on one founder, so a fast brand can cool swiftly. The debt from its acquisitions is manageable, but it limits e.l.f.'s room if growth slows. Keep the position smaller than you'd give a steadier name. Then watch whether growth holds without new deals, whether margins stay healthy, and whether new launches keep landing. If all three hold, build the position over time. If they don't, you've risked a small stake and not your conviction.

#119655. Your 401(k) Has Newly introduced Contribution Limits for 2027. Here's What You Need to Know

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (522 w)
📖 Baca

Your 401(k) Has Newly introduced Contribution Limits for 2027. Here's What You Need to Know

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, at this point, 401(k)s have become synonymous with retirement accounts because so many Americans have one.
  • Industry observers note that A 401(k) is a true win-win.
  • Beginning next year, you can contribute $25,500 to a 401(k), up from this year's $24,500 limit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Stefon Walters – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:30PM EST.

According to recent reports, at this point, 401(k)s have become synonymous with retirement accounts because so many Americans have one. It's by far the most used retirement account in the U.S., and it's why millions can have a financially comfortable retirement.

Industry observers note that A 401(k) is a true win-win. It helps you save and invest for retirement proactively, and you get a tax break for doing so. There are many moving parts to a 401(k), but one key rule to keep track of is the contribution limit. Let's dive into what to expect next year.

Beginning next year, you can contribute $25,500 to a 401(k), up from this year's $24,500 limit. If you're 50 or older, you can add an $8,500 catch-up contribution (up from $8,000), bringing your limit to $34,000.

According to recent reports, workers aged 60 to 63 can make a special catch-up contribution of up to $11,750, meaning anyone in that four-year age range can contribute $37,250 to their 401(k)s in 2027. Once you turn 64 or older, you go back to the standard catch-up amount.

The contribution limit applies only to your personal contributions. If your job matches a certain amount of your contributions, that match doesn't count against your limit. For example, if you're younger than 50 and your job matches up to $15,000 annually, you can also contribute $15,000, even though $30,000 is above the $25,500 limit for 2027.

Industry observers note that not many people can afford to max out their 401(k)s year in and year out, but you should try to contribute at least the amount your employer will match. It's essentially "free" money because it's a guaranteed instant 100% return on your investment. Don't leave it on the table.

IRA contribution limits often increase, but they're staying put next year. The contribution limit for IRAs -- both traditional and Roth combined -- is $7,500. People 50 or older can add a $1,100 catch-up contribution, bringing the limit to $8,600.

#119652. Latest Update: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1169 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1169 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities.
  • Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?
  • Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the latest reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Recent findings suggest that speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s new security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

In a recent development, according to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”.

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target.

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

According to recent reports, custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’.

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of new software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Industry observers note that threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, states cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

According to recent reports, bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a upcoming, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security issues, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

It has been revealed that also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are.

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security problems introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against upcoming and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance.

CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it rolled out the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

It has been revealed that apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, stated in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

It has been revealed that participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Recent findings suggest that apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now.

In a recent development, the AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which debuts officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google released its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

It has been revealed that A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

Recent findings suggest that “Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” stated Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this newly introduced health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

Also: Oura Ring consumers may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Proposal takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering fresh time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring consumers will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Initiative accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

In a recent development, after adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Recent findings suggest that go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Initiative to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

What Every 65-Year-Old Should Know About Social Security

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that age 65 can feel like a gray area for Social Security because it's a few years after you can start receiving benefits, but it's still before you reach your full retirement age.
  • But age 65 still matters because it affects Social Security benefits and has health insurance implications, so if you're nearing 65 or planning to claim at that age, here are a few things to know.
  • Sources indicate that you can begin claiming Social Security at age 62, but claiming any time before your full retirement age -- which is 67 for anyone born in 1960 or later -- will reduce your monthly benefit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Stefon Walters – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:30PM EST.

Industry observers note that age 65 can feel like a gray area for Social Security because it's a few years after you can start receiving benefits, but it's still before you reach your full retirement age. For a while, 65 was the traditional retirement age and seen as the "finish line," but that isn't necessarily the case today.

But age 65 still matters because it affects Social Security benefits and has health insurance implications, so if you're nearing 65 or planning to claim at that age, here are a few things to know.

Sources indicate that you can begin claiming Social Security at age 62, but claiming any time before your full retirement age -- which is 67 for anyone born in 1960 or later -- will reduce your monthly benefit. Your full retirement age is when you can receive your full monthly benefit, called your primary insurance amount. This is the starting point Social Security uses to determine your benefit based on when you claim.

Benefits are reduced by 5/9 of 1% monthly for each month you claim early, up to 36 months. So, if your full retirement age is 67 and you claim at 65, your benefit will be reduced by around 13.33%. If your full benefit was $2,000, you'd receive $1,733.33 if you claimed at 65.

In a recent development, if you claim benefits before your full retirement age, you could be subject to the Social Security retirement earnings test if you earn above a certain limit. For 2026, the limit is $24,480 if you won't reach your full retirement age in 2026 and $65,160 if you will. In 2027, these limits increase to $25,560 and $67,920, respectively.

In a recent development, if you earn above the limit in the year you won't reach full retirement age, your monthly benefit will be reduced by $1 for each $2 you're over. If you reach full retirement age that year and earn above the limit, your benefit is reduced by $1 per $3 you're over.

Thankfully, benefits aren't permanently lost -- just withheld. Once you reach your full retirement age, Social Security will gradually return the withheld benefits by increasing your monthly payout.

Industry observers note that social Security and Medicare are two different programs, but they're connected in how premiums are paid. You become eligible for Medicare at age 65, and if you're receiving Social Security at the time, your Medicare Part B premiums are automatically deducted from your monthly Social Security benefit.

According to recent reports, this year, the Medicare Part B premium is $202.90, but it will increase to $209.40 in 2027. If you claim both Social Security and Medicare and your monthly benefit is $2,000 next year, you'd receive $1,790.60 after the premium is deducted.

This automatic deduction applies only to Part B premiums. If you're enrolled in another Medicare strategy, such as Part C (Medicare Advantage) or Part D (prescriptions), you'll pay those premiums directly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in iOS 27, Apple declared iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows owners to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not right now support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that owners must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, customers will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

Recent findings suggest that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for owners with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple noted on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ prepares, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ strategy and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Sources indicate that advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

Industry observers note that one positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

According to recent reports, this all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

Sources indicate that how will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ initiative.

Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a new laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

We recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you blueprint to buy a new laptop while there are holiday savings.

Industry observers note that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple people saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

Apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

How much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

Sources indicate that if you proposal to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — presently MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

Sources indicate that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple owners stated their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

According to recent reports, digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple users seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Recent findings suggest that take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple people may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

Battery life is a major deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook owners saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

According to recent reports, comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo users say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test highlights that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its customers either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

Sources indicate that “Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” said Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook owners have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

It has been revealed that and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple users reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their complications. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

According to recent reports, our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

In a recent development, “Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” said Goldman.

It has been revealed that lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it states encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

When it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple consumers reported poor performance.

Industry observers note that here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without concerns or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

According to recent reports, on the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple people rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Industry observers note that apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple customers planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

It has been revealed that usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

Asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

If you’re planning to spend that amount on a new laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus customers say they’re extremely satisfied.

Asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice important must-have features for the price.

Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

Over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer customers say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.

If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a big 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.

Even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.

Lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.

Survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.

Goldman noted Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

Industry observers note that if your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a fresh laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners remarked they haven’t had any hardware concerns with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

Beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

If you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and new Space Frame design, which Elliott says makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.

According to recent reports, many Lenovo laptop users are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a latest laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.

Here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its new designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.

Asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.

Asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.

Asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.

It has been revealed that asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.

Sources indicate that for example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott stated. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.

Dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.

In a recent development, dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

According to recent reports, complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, revealed Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Recent findings suggest that because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick enhancement when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

As promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

According to recent reports, the interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook consumers and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac challenges as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

According to recent reports, back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

In a recent development, an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

According to recent reports, apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and users. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple users flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

For many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

Industry observers note that in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community customers to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others noted the site grew less helpful over the years.

CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he remarked.

Just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

According to recent reports, the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push people away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

In a recent development, reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual people to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

Apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The firm may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum users on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

Whatever the reason, the circle of Apple people helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Right now, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

Industry observers note that to correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both newly introduced settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

Recent findings suggest that chatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

According to recent reports, in all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the tech giant take this step in the right direction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:45PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Uber Technologies ›.

When looking at a list of the most innovative and disruptive businesses this century, the investment community will agree that Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) is impossible to ignore. It completely upended the taxi industry, leveraging the prevalence of smartphones, the app economy, and faster connectivity to become a global technology giant.

The impressive position Uber has built, however, hasn't prevented the growth stock from lagging the broader market in the past five years. And it now trades at what appears to be a very compelling forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.4, even though its financial performance is strong.

Management might be feeling the weight of the market's worries about the potential threat that autonomous vehicles (AV) will pose for the firm's operations. There's a valid argument to be made that this exciting latest technology could end up being a major opportunity for Uber, though. And that alters the investment thesis, signalling that shares are attractively priced right now.

When investors hear about developments within the AV industry, two companies come to mind. The market leader is Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Waymo. It's backed by one of the most dominant technology companies in the world, which means it has top-tier talent and software/hardware capabilities that are hard to beat.

Recent findings suggest that waymo is winning the race. The platform currently operates in 15 U.S. cities. There are intends to expand domestically, as well as in London and Tokyo. It completed 500,000 fully autonomous trips per week in March.

It has been revealed that there's also Tesla (TSLA -7.64%), which is winding down the Cybertruck to shift factory production to the two-seater Cybercab. Its robotaxi service offers full self-driving rides in eight U.S. cities. Despite a slow rollout, Elon Musk has high hopes.

Assuming that both Waymo and Tesla make rapid advancements in AV tech, expand to new markets, grow their user bases, increase miles driven, lower costs, successfully navigate a patchy regulatory environment, and maintain strict safety standards, then it's possible their ride-hailing apps more effectively compete with Uber's leadership position in mobility.

And that's the threat that's harming sentiment toward Uber stock. There is terminal risk from AVs.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sources indicate that uber is still operating at full strength. It ended the third quarter with 215 million monthly active owners. Mobility gross bookings jumped 18% year over year to $29.5 billion. And operating income was well over $1.4 billion, up 30%.

Sources indicate that the business has built up a powerful network effect, matching riders with drivers in cities around the globe. The key is that it directly controls demand and manages the customer relationship. That puts it in an advantageous position to essentially become the AV commercialization layer.

Sources indicate that if you're an AV software developer, auto manufacturer, or any other related technical provider, you've likely incurred sizable capital investments. And it's preferred that monetization happens sooner rather than later. Plugging into Uber's platform seems like the best solution to maximize vehicle utilization. it completed 4.1 billion trips just in the last three months.

Recent findings suggest that management isn't waiting around. It's actively partnering with AV companies, most notably with a total planned $10 billion capital commitment, to drive supply onto its network. It already invested in Rivian Automotive, Lucid Group, and Nuro, for instance. And it's entered into car purchasing agreements.

In a recent development, the company is targeting about 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform by year-end. By the end of 2027, it's aiming for more than 2,000. These are tiny figures in the grand scheme of things.

Uber believes that human drivers will also play a crucial role for a long time. This assumption is supported by the simple fact that rider demand fluctuates wildly depending on the time of day. Human drivers can handle demand spikes. If all rides were from AVs, on the other hand, many of these cars would be idle most of the time, which would be financially wasteful.

Recent findings suggest that still, it would be naive to think that Uber is in the clear. AVs pose a real long-term threat. It's something investors should monitor closely.

It has been revealed that however, the business is leaning on its favorable hand by setting itself up to remain a leader in mobility. The current valuation more than reflects the market's negative view.

It has been revealed that this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

In a recent development, the Chrome revision allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a fresh window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

In a recent development, the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

According to recent reports, also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these latest features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the latest features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the enhancement, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

  • Sources indicate that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • According to recent reports, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The fresh program expands on the company’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which rolled out in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

Sources indicate that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole new influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

According to recent reports, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

Sources indicate that first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

It has been revealed that as any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

According to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

In a recent development, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

Recent findings suggest that uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Sources indicate that google has declared that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

According to recent reports, if you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that says “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

Sources indicate that A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get owners familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

Recent findings suggest that first, you can now share any Skill with other people. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

Sources indicate that when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and enhancement in real time, Google states. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 2:51PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nike ›.

Choosing between Nike (NKE -4.11%) and Procter & Gamble (PG +0.91%) involves weighing the high-performance growth potential of athletic apparel against the defensive stability of household essentials as investors look toward 2027.

Nike dominates the footwear market by blending product innovation with powerful brand marketing, while Procter & Gamble operates a vast empire of daily necessities like soaps and detergents. Both companies offer immense global reach, but they serve different roles in a diversified portfolio, making it vital to understand their current financial health.

In a recent development, nike designs and sells athletic footwear and apparel globally, focusing on its Nike Direct business and a vast network of wholesale accounts. The organization utilizes a mix of retail stores and digital platforms to reach consumers in over 40 countries. In the United States, customer concentration is notable as the three largest customers account for roughly 29% of sales, which adds a layer of risk to the business.

According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Aug. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $45.9 billion, which was a decrease of approximately 1.2% from the previous twelve-month period. Despite this slight decline in sales, the firm generated a net income of roughly $3.1 billion. This performance resulted in a net margin of close to 6.7% for the period.

Recent findings suggest that as of its May 2026 balance sheet, the tech giant maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.7x. Debt-to-equity is a measure of total debt relative to shareholder equity, indicating how much the company relies on borrowing to fund its operations. The current ratio is roughly 2.0x, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term liabilities with short-term assets. In the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026, free cash flow was approximately $2.2 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 24.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Industry observers note that procter & Gamble manages a diverse portfolio of essential brands, operating as a leader among consumer staples stocks across categories like healthcare and family care. The organization sells these daily necessities through various channels, including grocery stores, pharmacies, and mass merchandisers. A significant portion of its business is concentrated with Walmart (WMT +1.51%), which accounts for approximately 16% of total sales.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $87.9 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 3.5% compared to the prior period. This consistent performance resulted in a net income of nearly $16.0 billion for the year. High net margin levels of roughly 18.2% highlight the manufacturer's ability to maintain profitability while navigating fluctuating costs.

According to recent reports, as of its June 2026 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.6x. Debt-to-equity is a measure of total debt relative to shareholder equity, and this level suggests a moderate use of borrowing. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term debts with assets it can quickly convert to cash, is approximately 0.7x. In the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, free cash flow was close to $15.1 billion.

Sources indicate that nike faces intense global competition from various athletic and lifestyle footwear and apparel companies such as adidas (ADDDF -6.04%) and Under Armour (UAA -1.56%). The company relies heavily on a concentrated base of contract manufacturers and suppliers located outside the United States, which creates vulnerability to supply chain disruptions. Additionally, volatility in global economic conditions and a significant reliance on complex information technology systems pose ongoing operational risks.

Procter & Gamble contends with significant competition across diverse product categories from both global competitors and private-label brands. The tech giant is dependent on complex global supply chains and faces constant pressure from fluctuations in the costs of commodities, energy, and transportation. Furthermore, managing compliance with a wide array of global legal, regulatory, and tax requirements remains a primary challenge for the organization.

Procter & Gamble currently offers a lower valuation based on future earnings estimates, while Nike provides a lower entry point based on its P/S ratio.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with Procter & Gamble. It owns the everyday brands like Tide, Pampers, and Gillette that people buy again and again, and it turns that loyalty into steady cash for shareholders. P&G has raised its dividend for an incredible 70 straight years and has paid one for well over a century. What really stands out to me right now is how broad the growth is. Sales rose 4% in its latest quarter, above what the firm had guided for the year, and all five of its business segments grew.

To give Nike its due, its running and other sports businesses are growing, and it has a CEO working to win back customers. But there's no way around it: Nike's business is in a tough spot right now. It expects sales to fall this fiscal year as it cuts back some lifestyle shoes and overhauls how it sells in China.

Sources indicate that P&G, by contrast, is growing from a very steady base. For long-term investors, that mix of trusted brands, steady growth, and a rising dividend makes P&G the better buy for 2027.
