10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

Anthropic's (ANT -8.50%) IPO was a smashing success. It broke the 5-month-old record for the biggest IPO ever and opened well above its IPO price. Clearly, many investors and analysts are excited about the firm's prospects, and that is already being reflected in various price targets. For instance, Scott Berg, an analyst at Needham & Company, initiated coverage of the stock with a $150 price target. That implies an almost 72% upside from current levels. Could Anthropic really rise that much over the next year?

In a recent development, at a stock price of $150, Anthropic's market cap would be about $2 trillion (it would be higher on a fully diluted basis). That would put the tech company in a very exclusive group. Here is an argument as to why this valuation could make sense, especially in 12 months, once we have more data on Anthropic's performance.

First, the company's revenue has been growing at a dizzying pace. Third-quarter revenue was $17 billion, up 1,127% year over year. Anthropic's run rate revenue grew by $10 billion in a single month, to $81 billion as of the end of October.

According to recent reports, true, the tech giant remains unprofitable. In the third quarter, its net loss was $23.3 billion, significantly worse than the $12.1 billion loss recorded in the prior-year quarter. But that was mostly due to non-cash charges driven by an increase in the value of various financial instruments -- a mostly paper loss that tells us very little about the fundamentals of Anthropic's business.

Meanwhile, several factors could allow the manufacturer's growth to maintain a strong pace. Anthropic arguably benefits from a competitive edge. For instance, with about 40 million users across its portfolio of AI-powered tools, including more than 1,900 customers with trailing 12-month revenue exceeding $1 million, Anthropic is building network effects.

It has been revealed that data and customer feedback can help the company improve its AI-powered tools and attract even more owners. The company also argues that more sophisticated versions of its Claude frontier model will help it build even better ones next time around, strengthening its lead. Claude has been writing increasingly more code per person within the company.

Embedding this AI tool into Anthropic's workflows could lead to significant productivity gains in the medium term and allow the organization to reduce expenses and turn a profit. Based on the company's run rate revenue and the pace at which it is growing, it could reach sales well above $100 billion in fiscal year 2027.

Suppose Anthropic records $115 billion in revenue next year and ends 2027 with a $150 stock price. The tech giant's price-to-sales ratio as of the end of the year would be 17.3 on a basic-share count basis. If, in addition, the company can turn a profit, that valuation wouldn't be that unreasonable.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that however, there is significant uncertainty. Consider, for instance, that Anthropic revealed $900.9 billion in infrastructure commitments with various companies. What's more, many of those agreements are non-cancellable.

The message management is sending here is clear. Anthropic is bullish on the future of AI. But if spending on the technology declines meaningfully, that would be a massive blow to the company. Revenue growth would decline, making it much more challenging for Anthropic to post consistent profits.

There are other potential problems. Other AI companies might steal some of its business as corporations increasingly seek to diversify their portfolio of AI-powered tools away from the largest providers. Or perhaps Anthropic might fail to maintain its rapid pace of technological progress, leading to a decline in market share.

These are all meaningful risks to keep in mind, though some might not matter over the next 12 months. Still, they matter to long-term investors, and the question isn't just whether Anthropic stock could rise to $150 by the end of 2027 -- it's whether the manufacturer could deliver exceptional returns over the long run. I am not yet convinced that it will; that's why I am staying away for now.

But Anthropic is worth keeping on investors' watchlists, at the right price, which, in my view, is around the $83 IPO price, or slightly below it for a healthy margin of error.

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

In a recent development, salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Industry observers note that brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Recent findings suggest that shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

Sources indicate that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Recent findings suggest that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Recent findings suggest that agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent customers using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

In a recent development, the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

In a recent development, retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

It has been revealed that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

It has been revealed that if you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it. While Claude — our top pick for AI chatbots — is one of the better options when it comes to privacy, the default settings can still leave something to be desired if you value yours.

Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.

Industry observers note that by default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most important setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

The settings essentially remain the same across web, iOS and Android:.

You may not see this option because with some accounts, like Enterprise plans, Claude doesn’t automatically collect this data. So if you have a Claude account through work, you might not have to worry about this.

While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training.

Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

According to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.).

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

Recent findings suggest that if you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

Recent findings suggest that this will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating latest memories from your conversations:.

If you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

However, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

As with most agentic products, more frequent people may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

One of the most fascinating parts of Berkshire Hathaway's sprawling business is its roughly $360 billion equity portfolio, in which the company invests the float generated by its insurance business in a wide range of stocks across sectors.

In his more than six decades as CEO of Berkshire, Warren Buffett built one of the best investing track records in history. He has since passed the torch to new CEO Greg Abel, a longtime Berkshire veteran and close confidant of Buffett, who plans to continue Buffett's remarkably concentrated approach to investing.

Industry observers note that to this day, just three stocks make up nearly 47% of Berkshire's portfolio. Perhaps even more amazing is that none of these three are traditional artificial intelligence hyperscalers.

It has been revealed that while Berkshire's investment moves are a strong starting point, investors should realize that Berkshire rarely explains its positions. Its filings arrive with a delay, so treat them as a starting point for your own research, not a shopping list.

Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

Apple (AAPL -1.90%) is Berkshire's largest position by a wide margin. The roughly 228 million shares haven't changed in four straight quarterly filings, a notable pause after Buffett trimmed the stake for nearly two years.

Buffett, Abel, and the Berkshire team probably like Apple due to its loyal customer base of more than 2.5 billion active devices, high-margin Services revenue, and massive share repurchases over the past decade-plus that have significantly reduced Apple's outstanding shares, thereby increasing Berkshire's slice of profits.

Apple repurchased $24 billion of stock in its latest quarter, on top of a new $100 billion authorization declared in the spring.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

With a market capitalization above $5 trillion, Apple is now the largest stock in the world by market value. The results back it up: Fiscal 2026 revenue hit a record $478.8 billion, up 15%, and earnings per share rose 20% to $8.98. September-quarter iPhone revenue set a record, and services revenue also reached an all-time high of $31.6 billion.

Recent findings suggest that trading around 39 times trailing earnings, Apple stock isn't cheap. It has a new CEO, John Ternus, and shareholders are keen to ensure the manufacturer can keep producing innovative consumer tech products.

Apple is also in an enviable position: It's not investing hundreds of billions in data centers and therefore not experiencing issues with free cash flow. Furthermore, Apple's leadership in consumer tech hardware, such as the iPhone, means it is likely to play a major role in delivering artificial intelligence to the public.

Berkshire has held American Express (AXP -3.02%) since the early 1990s and owns more than 22% of the tech giant. Amex has a fantastic brand and business model that are difficult to replicate.

Amex is both a credit card issuer and a payments network, meaning it extends credit to consumers and businesses and facilitates transactions between customers and merchants.

According to recent reports, when run well, the credit card business can generate strong returns on capital, and Amex caters to a more affluent customer base that is typically more resilient during recessions. Meanwhile, the payments business generates capital-light recurring fee revenue. In the third quarter, net card fee growth accelerated to 17% year over year.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, however, the stock has struggled this year, lagging the S&P 500 as investors worry about stablecoins and regulatory pressure on card economics. The business, however, is doing fine. Q3 revenue hit a record $20.1 billion, up 9%. Billed business rose 8% to $454 billion, and Amex raised its full-year earnings guidance.

Berkshire hasn't touched its Amex position since the 1990s, so Abel and the team clearly do not share current investor concerns.

Recent findings suggest that coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) may be the most Buffett stock of all. Berkshire has owned it since 1988 and holds 400 million shares. With the quarterly dividend now $0.53 per share, those shares generate roughly $848 million in annual dividends. The tech giant has raised its payout for 64 consecutive years.

Abel and his team likely value many of the attributes that have always made the iconic beverage company attractive: global brands, pricing power, and steady cash flow. Management expects at least $13 billion in free cash flow this year.

The stock has been a big winner this year, as investors rotate somewhat out of artificial intelligence and tech and into the best-in-breed consumer staples stock.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In Q3, unit case volume at the manufacturer grew 5%, organic revenue rose 7%, and comparable earnings per share climbed 11%. After the strong run this year, Coca-Cola is no longer cheap, trading over 29 times forward earnings.

So while upside may be capped in the near term, Coca-Cola can generate solid long-term returns through the business cycle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the manufacturer would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Significant Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the firm is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, stated in 2023 that the organization’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

Recent findings suggest that meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the organization says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

It has been revealed that take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its newly introduced data center designs compared to its original ones.

It has been revealed that but, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple is kicking off a latest and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

It has been revealed that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

A new feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

It has been revealed that with a new feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

The new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the fresh Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the newly introduced features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
  • Take Southwest Airlines, for example.
  • "Experiences create lifetime memories,” claims Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

Take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

"Experiences create lifetime memories,” claims Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

Southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but big-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

It has been revealed that even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

Recent findings suggest that four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

In a recent development, if you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

Recent findings suggest that daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

It has been revealed that ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

Again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

It has been revealed that grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

The biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

It has been revealed that you’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

With that said, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Sources indicate that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

Industry observers note that finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

Recent findings suggest that but every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Industry observers note that personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” says Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (871 w)

Does Anthropic Have a Competitive Advantage? These are the Four Significant Ones

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) just made stock market history with its IPO.
  • At $91.6 billion, the organization raised more cash in its debut than any company before it.
  • The organization had the misfortune of going public while the broader AI sector is crashing on fears surrounding Nvidia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) just made stock market history with its IPO.

At $91.6 billion, the organization raised more cash in its debut than any company before it. That would seem to be a bullish sign for the stock, but after an initial pop, Anthropic closed Friday trading just 7% above its IPO price, and at one point the stock was trading just five cents above the $83 listing price.

The organization had the misfortune of going public while the broader AI sector is crashing on fears surrounding Nvidia. Anthropic also has plenty of skeptics, who have called out risks like the $900 billion it has in purchase commitments, falling token prices, competition from cheaper models, and concerns about circular financing in the industry involving Nvidia.

Those risks are all valid, but the company has also reported revenue growth of 1,200% year-over-year through the first three quarters of the year, and it's already reached a revenue run rate of $68 billion. No company this young has ever been this significant. Over the longer term, Anthropic sees its technology playing a role in everything from curing diseases to designing chips to making robots and beyond. In other words, it's a high-risk, high-reward stock.

Anthropic is in a newly introduced, rapidly evolving industry, and one of the most pressing questions for investors at this point is whether it has a sustainable competitive advantage.

It has been revealed that investors typically look for one of four types of competitive advantage. Those include:.

Anthropic clearly isn't the low-cost provider. It's a frontier AI lab running on state-of-the-art chips from Nvidia and others. Distillation models like DeepSeek's R1 are an example of low-cost providers in generative AI.

Anthropic's brand is getting stronger and becoming more of a competitive advantage. Claude, its core intelligence platform and chatbot, now rivals OpenAI's ChatGPT in recognition, and its other products like Claude Cowork and Claude Code have become well-known as well. Anthropic's brand helps attract new owners and keep existing ones. If Anthropic's brand is recognized as the best AI, that gives it a competitive advantage.

At an enterprise level, switching costs do apply to a product like Claude, as they do to the rest of the software industry. A business that's paid for hundreds or even thousands of Claude seats is going to face friction if it wants to switch to another provider. At the individual consumer level, switching costs are minimal.

Network effects do not really apply to AI, as it isn't used to connect with other users.

Of these four, brand seems like Anthropic's best opportunity to build a competitive advantage, much like Apple's in smartphones and consumer electronics.

Technology on its own isn't generally considered a source of sustainable competitive advantage, especially in a rapidly evolving field like AI. Anthropic took the lead from OpenAI in part by introducing more capable models, but the race between the two companies continues, and Anthropic is not guaranteed to maintain its lead.

Technology can help build a competitive advantage when it's combined with patents or trade secrets, regulatory barriers to entry, or a strong brand, and it's clearly a major reason for Anthropic's meteoric growth.

Being the technology leader in an industry is a competitive advantage, but it's often not seen as sustainable.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Anthropic sees its competitive advantage stemming from the flywheel below, which shows how its usage improves its models, similar to Google Search, and also drives more investment, which makes its models better.

In a recent development, anthropic's flywheels. Image source: Anthropic.

What Anthropic describes here is more about how its business model creates a flywheel that makes it better, rather than a true competitive advantage.

For a market leader, however, this kind of flywheel can drive a competitive advantage, as it has for Google Search, which learns and improves from the way consumers use the product.

It has been revealed that I don't think it's correct to say that Anthropic doesn't have a competitive advantage, even though none of the four main ones strongly apply. I think the combination of its brand, technology, and the improvement flywheels constitutes an emerging competitive advantage that will be tested over the coming months and years.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

#119575. Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📖 Baca

Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
  • The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
  • Industry observers note that that threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker said these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

Industry observers note that that threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

According to recent reports, whittaker remarked that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the company is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

Sources indicate that the problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal indicates that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

Whittaker mentioned the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

In a recent development, “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker noted. “This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

According to recent reports, “So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” noted Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand said the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

In a recent development, employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report demonstrates how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse noted, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson mentioned.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor.

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report remarked.

Sources indicate that but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the organization, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Recent findings suggest that samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

Sources indicate that “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most notable decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse remarked.

Recent findings suggest that A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

Industry observers note that “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson stated. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

#119571. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (769 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
  • According to recent reports, it’s an exciting time for NASA.
  • Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

According to recent reports, it’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other massive win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s Upcoming Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the manufacturer was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Recent findings suggest that escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

In a recent development, by the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

Recent findings suggest that the tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

It has been revealed that “With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a newly introduced strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, mentioned in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

Recent findings suggest that the maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, rolled out its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX introduced, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

Sources indicate that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

In a recent development, non-electronic toys are a good bet, states Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

Recent findings suggest that neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold indicates.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

Industry observers note that “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” indicates Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley states.

Sources indicate that got some counter space and an itch for a newly introduced food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

According to recent reports, “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath claims. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold states.

Sources indicate that electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath notes.

It has been revealed that gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath states. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That mentioned, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold claims.

For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, notes consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Newly introduced Year’s Day.

“Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

Sources indicate that many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold notes. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Sources indicate that just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath notes. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch says.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch states. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

It has been revealed that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley notes. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero.
  • According to recent reports, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use.
  • Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

According to recent reports, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

It could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Sources indicate that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this upcoming platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

It has been revealed that the Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends.
  • Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.
  • New to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

New to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is at the moment rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a upcoming thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s upcoming Skills.

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google states:.

According to recent reports, “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google noted on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

Sources indicate that for those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

According to recent reports, chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google revealed that it would be rolling out new settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

There are two tiers to choose from with the newly introduced bundles: a Value plan, which runs $28 per month (in addition to any monthly live TV subscription fees) and carries Netflix Standard with Ads, HBO Max’s ad-based plan and Apple TV, or the Deluxe plan, an ad-free option that costs $43.50 a month and includes Netflix Standard, HBO Max Standard and Apple TV. Either bundle can be added to or canceled from your existing plan at any time.

Right now, if you want to watch all the best demonstrates, live sports and news programs, they’re scattered across multiple services, and this bundle offers you three of the most robust services out there, while skirting their latest price increases.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

In a recent development, so too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this latest take on the OS is the epitome of that.

It has been revealed that the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with newly introduced ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

The developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

It has been revealed that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

Sources indicate that at the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

In a recent development, once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

Industry observers note that as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One problem that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

According to recent reports, I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

Recent findings suggest that it would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

Sources indicate that you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my upcoming favorite free productivity suite.

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

According to recent reports, investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.
