📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

If PCE highlights inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index revealed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

Sources indicate that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

It has been revealed that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

According to recent reports, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

According to recent reports, » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

According to recent reports, 🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Procter & Gamble ›.

The most interesting thing Procter & Gamble (PG +0.91%) made this year might be a diaper.

Recent findings suggest that it's called Pampers Amoira, P&G's most premium diaper yet. It was built on a simple insight: Families are having fewer babies, so parents are willing to spend more on each one. CFO Andre Schulten stated Amoira is on track to top $100 million in U.S. sales in its first year.

That one product states a lot about where P&G is headed, and it's why I'd want to own the stock before 2027. The 70-year dividend streak is just the bonus.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Jejurikar, a P&G lifer who joined in 1989, became CEO on Jan. 1. He isn't tearing up the strategy so much as changing how it's carried out. P&G is spending more time in shoppers' homes, making brand content for algorithm-driven social feeds, and working with retailers on everything from store displays to AI shopping tools.

According to recent reports, it's working so far. Organic sales rose 4% last quarter, mostly because people bought more products rather than paid higher prices. "Growth going forward is not about taking share. Growth going forward is about growing our categories," Schulten said.

Industry observers note that P&G also bought Thorne, a premium supplements brand. "It's a really well-run operation, and it's been around for a long time," Jejurikar told CNBC.

The biggest reason is a restructuring program that cuts up to 7,000 non-manufacturing jobs and exits some weaker brands and markets over two fiscal years. Schulten called it "an important step toward ensuring our ability to deliver our long-term algorithm over the coming two to three years." In this year's annual report letter, Jejurikar wrote that P&G is "committed to improving results semester by semester and year by year.".

The road there runs through higher oil prices, though. "Due to the duration of higher oil prices, we now expect materially higher cost headwinds in Q2 and the second half of fiscal 2027," Schulten warned, and P&G is "closely watching consumer demand as high fuel and energy costs persist into the fall and winter." That's partly why P&G expects core earnings growth of just 0% to 3% this fiscal year, and its pricing power is limited, since price increases had only a minor effect on sales last quarter.

At about 26 times earnings and near its 52-week high, the stock also carries a full P/E ratio for a tech giant growing earnings in the low single digits.

According to recent reports, still, I'd rather own P&G while the hard work is happening than wait until the payoff is obvious. Trusted brands, a leaner cost base, and new products like Amoira are the kind of economic moat that rewards patience. Buying before the savings show up beats paying up once everyone can see them.

Recent findings suggest that on its third-quarter 2026 business update call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Stoke Therapeutics (STOK -0.45%) announced alignment with the FDA on a composite endpoint for lead drug candidate Zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome. This regulatory agreement clarifies the approval pathway for the experimental medicine, which targets a rare genetic epilepsy with high unmet medical need. For long-term investors, clear clinical endpoints and full trial retention strengthen prospects for potential approval and launch in early 2028.

Three things management remarked stand out.

The Newly introduced Drug Application (NDA) submission for Zorevunersen, an investigational therapy for Dravet syndrome, will use a combined cognitive and behavioral assessment. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) agreed to evaluate key secondary endpoints using four subdomains from Vineland-3, an adaptive behavior scale.

Industry observers note that in the EMPEROR Phase III registrational trial, 162 patients enrolled across global sites without a single participant dropping out. High patient retention preserves statistical power and signals strong caregiver commitment to the clinical program.

Management identified 6,000 addressable pediatric patients in the U.S. living with Dravet syndrome. Half of those patients receive treatment at 50 specialized medical centers experienced in intrathecal delivery, an injection directly into the spinal canal.

Clinical progress extends into autosomal dominant optic atrophy, an inherited disorder causing vision loss. Phase I dosing for STK-002 tests whether targeting protein deficiency translates into improved sight.

Cash reserves of $358.8 million and partner reimbursements provide multiyear funding through expected commercial launch.

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1381 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

It has been revealed that these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

According to recent reports, some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s crucial to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

It has been revealed that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Industry observers note that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

In a recent development, even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

It has been revealed that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

According to recent reports, which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Recent findings suggest that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

According to recent reports, apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

It has been revealed that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

In a recent development, not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.
